labels.label: bzprop:c3s2p2_alpha_somme
labels.notes: Checked against benzecri1960_ch3.tex l.365-377, sec. 2 Def. 1 (l.299-309) and sec. 1 Def. 1 (l.91-95). Anchor Benzecri.alphaW_somme_iff: [Fintype I], IsSommeConvexes W V (W and every V_i convex, sum map an affine isomorphism of prod V_i onto W, which is exactly sec. 2 Def. 1 with I finite), arbitrary families x y : I -> E with x i, y i in V i; conclusion AlphaW W (sum x) (sum y) <-> forall i, AlphaW (V i) (x i) (y i). No hypothesis added: x, y in W follows from the sums, and by uniqueness of the decomposition any such family is the components (alphaW_iff_composante states it with the components of x, y in W). AlphaW is sec. 1 Def. 1 as printed (open-segment clause or A = B and A in W). The 'cf. def. 1' reading (sec. 1 Def. 1, OQ-160 (b)) is disclosed in SCOPE and in REPORT questions; the transcription's \ref already points at bzdef:c3s1d1_preordre_alpha, so the reading does not change the statement. The infinite form alphaW_sommeInfinie_iff (IsSommeInfinie) is disclosed as resting on T-bz-c3-sommes's reading of Remarque 2 and is correctly not the anchor. Instance Benzecri.exemple_carre_alpha is a real proof: it uses exemple_carre_somme (IsSommeConvexes of [0,1]^2 with the same V as in the instance), shows the componentwise relations directly by alphaW_iff_extend, and derives both the positive case (centre alpha(W) vertex) and the negative case (vertex not alpha(W) centre) through alphaW_somme_iff, so both directions of the anchor are exercised on a nondegenerate sum. The bold mark is honest: full statement, no sorry, standard axioms.
